doc.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023

title: Weekly gig at Hotel Vermont and the value of real-world gigs
summary: Vega plays Wednesdays at Hotel Vermont for ten years; Rowe says such gigs teach musicians to observe their audience and are rarer now.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Yeah but the other thing is I think you’re doing something that some of them don’t have the opportunity in that you’re playing things like you play at the Vermont Hotel is that correct?
Every Wednesday at the Hotel Vermont. We’ve been doing that for ten years except for the little hiccup with Covid, but ten years of jazz.

I think that kind of gig is so important for musicians because it’s real life for God’s sake and you learn to play, you learn to observe your audience that they’re not twenty feet away in a whole row of chairs you know in this big auditorium —
They’re right in front of you.
who are self-editing and I’m not sure what my point is but I feel a little sorry for the younger musicians because those gigs seem to be fewer and farther between these days.
